## §1.1 Sets and Functions

### Narrative

This section establishes the language we use throughout the book. Students should know this material from a proofs course; we collect it here for reference. The section is intentionally brief — definitions and notation, minimal scaffolding.

### Content

**Sets**
- Definition: set, element
- Notation: x ∈ A, x ∉ A
- Set-builder notation: {x : P(x)}
- Standard sets: ℕ = {1, 2, 3, ...}, ℤ = {..., −1, 0, 1, ...}, ℚ = {p/q : p, q ∈ ℤ, q ≠ 0}
- Subsets: A ⊆ B
- Equality: A = B means A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A

**Set Operations**
- Union: A ∪ B
- Intersection: A ∩ B
- Difference: A \ B
- Cartesian product: A × B
- Power set: 𝒫(A) = {S : S ⊆ A}

**Functions**
- Definition: f: A → B assigns to each element of A exactly one element of B
- Domain, codomain, range (image)
- Remark: functions are assignments, not formulas
- Notation: f: A → B, x ↦ f(x)

**Types of Functions**
- Injective (one-to-one): f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⟹ x₁ = x₂
- Surjective (onto): every y ∈ B is hit
- Bijective: both injective and surjective

**Operations on Functions**
- Composition: g ∘ f
- Inverse: f⁻¹ when f is bijective
- Theorem: f has an inverse iff f is bijective

**Cardinality**
- Definition: A and B have the same cardinality if there exists a bijection A → B
- Definition: A is countable if A is finite or has the same cardinality as ℕ
- Definition: A is uncountable if A is not countable
- Theorem (Cantor): There is no surjection A → 𝒫(A)
- Remark: This is the source of multiple sizes of infinity

### Guided Exercises

None for this section.

### Exercises

- Prove (A ∪ B) \ C = (A \ C) ∪ (B \ C)
- Prove A \ (B ∪ C) = (A \ B) ∩ (A \ C)
- Show f: A → B is bijective iff there exists g: B → A with g ∘ f = id_A and f ∘ g = id_B
- Prove Cantor's theorem: there is no surjection A → 𝒫(A)
- Show ℕ × ℕ is countable
- Show ℚ is countable

### Dependencies

**Requires**: Nothing — this is foundational language.

**Used in**: Throughout. Specific callbacks will be added as we outline later sections.
